digest.headline: The Nasdaq plunged 2.6% and Brent crude topped $112 a barrel as geopolitical conflicts sparked global risk aversion.

lede.b: The Nasdaq index dropped by 2.6% because people worried more about artificial intelligence and growing wars, which is a big drop in the price of technology company shares. Treasury yields, which are the return governments pay people who lend them money by buying their bonds, suffered their biggest single-day fall since the banking crisis of 2023. This happened as oil prices surged with Brent crude rising above $112 a barrel, making investors rush to safe places to keep their money. Meta shares fell heavily during the wider technology sell-off.
lede.i: The Nasdaq index tumbled 2.6% in its worst session since June amid revived doubts over artificial intelligence and escalating geopolitical conflicts. Treasury yields dropped sharply in their largest single-day fall since the banking crisis of 2023 as investors sought safe-haven assets. This flight to safety followed a surge in oil prices that pushed Brent crude above $112 a barrel.
lede.a: The Nasdaq suffered a 2.6% drawdown, marking its worst session since June as artificial intelligence skepticism and escalating conflict risk converged. Concurrently, Treasury yields registered their largest single-day compression since the 2023 banking crisis, driven by macroeconomic risk aversion. This flight to safety accompanied a surge in oil prices, with Brent crude topping $112 a barrel.

thread.b: Global markets dropped as oil prices climbed over $112 a barrel and technology shares sold off. Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure faced attacks and oil prices rose. This caused safe-haven assets to see heavy demand.
thread.i: Escalating regional conflicts pushed Brent crude above $112 a barrel and triggered a broad sell-off in technology equities. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East disrupted energy infrastructure and reduced risk appetite worldwide. Safe-haven assets attracted heavy inflows as equity benchmarks fell across multiple continents.
thread.a: Energy supply shocks driven by Middle Eastern infrastructure attacks propelled Brent crude above $112 a barrel, reinforcing macro risk aversion. Concurrently, co-ordinated technology liquidations across global exchanges compressed equity valuations. Safe-haven flows absorbed capital as cross-asset correlations reflected heightened geopolitical risk.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Nasdaq tumbles and Treasury yields drop sharply

stories.t: Nasdaq Suffers Sharp Losses
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list of shares tracked together to show how a part of the market is doing. The Nasdaq fell by 2.6% in its worst session since June. Tech stocks like Meta dropped heavily. Concerns about artificial intelligence and rising war jitters caused the selloff.
stories.i: The Nasdaq suffered its worst session since June with a 2.6% drop. Revived doubts over artificial intelligence and escalating war jitters sparked a broad technology selloff. Meta shares plummeted alongside other major tech names during the risk-off move.
stories.a: The Nasdaq composite tumbled 2.6% in its worst single-session performance since June. Renewed skepticism regarding artificial intelligence investments compounded geopolitical risk-off sentiment. Heavyweight constituents like Meta experienced steep declines as market participants rotated away from growth equities.

stories.t: Treasury Yields Fall Sharply
stories.b: Treasury yields are the return the government pays people who lend it money, like the interest on a loan. Yields logged their biggest drop since the banking crisis in 2023. Investors moved money as sentiment shifted.
stories.i: Treasury yields recorded their largest single-day drop since the banking crisis of 2023. The sudden movement followed a surge in oil prices, with Brent topping $112 a barrel. Macroeconomic risk aversion drove demand for safe-haven assets.
stories.a: United States Treasury yields registered their steepest decline since the 2023 banking crisis. Macroeconomic cross-currents driven by rising Brent crude prices above $112 a barrel catalyzed aggressive duration buying. Fixed-income instruments absorbed substantial capital as risk sentiment deteriorated across major asset classes.

politics.b: United States markets reacted to global events and technology sector drops on October 22, 2026.
politics.i: United States equities and fixed income reacted to shifting artificial intelligence sentiment and oil price spikes on October 22, 2026.
politics.a: United States financial markets priced in heightened volatility across technology equities and sovereign debt on October 22, 2026.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: U.K. inflation data and equity market movements

stories.t: Consumer Prices Accelerate as Rate Hike Pressure Builds
stories.b: The rate at which prices go up across the country is called inflation. When this number increases faster, things cost more. The latest data shows this measure jumped up again. This increase makes people think interest rates might go up. Interest rates are the cost of borrowing money.
stories.i: The U.K. inflation rate jumped again in the latest official figures. This acceleration strengthens the case for a central bank rate hike. Higher borrowing costs typically cool demand across the economy. Analysts now re-evaluate their monetary policy expectations following the release.
stories.a: U.K. inflation printed higher sequentially, forcing a repricing of terminal rate expectations. The renewed upward momentum in consumer prices compresses real yields and strengthens the hawkish policy narrative. Markets must now reconcile this sticky print against growth dynamics.

stories.t: FTSE 100 Slips Amid Declines in Banking and Mining Sectors
stories.b: The main stock market index is a group of big company shares traded together. The FTSE 100 is the main index in London. It dropped by 0.26% to reach 10,725.03. Companies like Barclays and various mining firms pulled the index down.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index slipped 0.26% to close at 10,725.03. Declines in Barclays and major mining equities dragged the benchmark lower. Conversely, Rentokil outperformed the broader market with a jump of more than 8%.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 retreated 0.26% to 10,725.03 under the weight of underperforming banking and basic resource names. Barclays and mining constituents exerted negative pressure on the capital-weighted index. Rentokil decoupled from the broader trend, rallying upwards of 8%.

politics.b: Financial regulators in the United Kingdom shared new plans. They want to make the rules for senior managers simpler. Fewer financial services jobs will need these extra checks.
politics.i: Financial regulators unveiled proposals to simplify the Senior Manager and Certification Regime. The total number of financial services roles facing enhanced regulatory checks will fall significantly. These proposed changes aim to support wider economic growth.
politics.a: Regulators published a framework to streamline the Senior Manager and Certification Regime. The scope of roles subjected to enhanced regulatory certification contracts sharply. This structural adjustment intends to reduce compliance friction and support sectoral growth.

timeline: Regulators unveil plans to simplify the Senior Manager and Certification Regime.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX index falls as Frankfurt markets close lower

stories.t: Frankfurt Stocks Fall
stories.b: Germany's main stock market index, the DAX 40, dropped 1.07% to close at 25,371.75. An index is a group of shares tracked together to show how a market is doing. Share prices fell across Frankfurt during the trading session. Infineon led the downward move in the market selloff. The DAX 40 ended the day in negative territory at 25,371.75.
stories.i: The DAX 40 index fell 1.07% to finish the session at 25,371.75. Equities across Frankfurt retreated as selling pressure intensified. Infineon led the losses in the broader market selloff. Trading activity pushed the index down to 25,371.75 by the close.
stories.a: The DAX 40 contracted 1.07% to settle at 25,371.75. Equity valuations in Frankfurt compressed amid broad-based selling. Infineon acted as the primary drag during the session. The index closed the day down at 25,371.75.

politics.b: No political updates were reported for Germany today.
politics.i: No political updates were reported for Germany today.
politics.a: No political updates were reported for Germany today.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Japanese markets drop on AI sell-off as the yen climbs

stories.t: Nikkei Sinks as Technology Stocks Face Sell-Off
stories.b: The Nikkei index tracks the value of large companies in Japan. This index dropped by 1,713 points. Stock prices fell because investors grew worried about spending on artificial intelligence. Major technology companies like Meta saw their share values sink.
stories.i: The Nikkei index tumbled by 1,713 points as a global sell-off hit technology shares. Heavy spending on artificial intelligence buildout bills pressured valuations across major tech favorites. Meta and similar tech equities absorbed steep losses during the session.
stories.a: The Nikkei plummeted 1,713 points as escalating capital expenditure concerns for artificial intelligence infrastructure triggered broad equity liquidations. Mega-cap technology equities bore the brunt of the risk-off rotation. Margin pressures from heavy buildout costs compressed valuations across key sector proxies like Meta.

stories.t: Japanese Yen Rises as Global Markets Seek Safety
stories.b: The Japanese yen is the official currency of Japan. Currency traders bought the yen because they wanted a safe place to put their money. Global markets turned cautious due to worries about politics and the economy.
stories.i: The Japanese yen surged against major foreign exchange counterparts. Global risk aversion intensified as traders sought safe-haven assets. Market participants reacted to political unrest in France and upcoming United States midterm elections.
stories.a: The Japanese yen rallied across major foreign exchange pairings as systemic risk aversion dominated macro flows. Heightened geopolitical uncertainty stemming from French unrest and looming United States midterm elections drove safe-haven capital into the currency. Market participants aggressively unwound risk-correlated positions.

politics.b: The Japanese government announced plans to lower financial support payments for eco-friendly vehicles next year. Officials also decided to create centralized support systems to promote anime and video games overseas.
politics.i: State authorities prepared to reduce consumer subsidies for eco-friendly vehicles starting next year. Separately, the government organized centralized support frameworks to promote anime and games in international markets.
politics.a: Policymakers finalized measures to scale back purchase subsidies for eco-friendly vehicles in the upcoming year. State apparatuses simultaneously established centralized promotion channels to drive overseas expansion for domestic anime and gaming sectors.

Japan schedules the release of domestic inflation data for Friday morning.

China.label: China
China.sub: Wealth market size, yuan trajectory and AI fund metrics

stories.t: China Wealth Sector and Exchange Rates
stories.b: China's bank wealth management market reached 35.4 trillion yuan. Think of this as the total pool of savings that everyday people give to banks to invest for them. Meanwhile, analysts at UOB project that the Chinese yuan will make gradual gains toward 6.6640 against the US dollar. A currency exchange rate is the price of one country's money in terms of another.
stories.i: China's bank wealth management market expanded to 35.4 trillion yuan. Simultaneously, UOB forecasters see the Chinese yuan heading for gradual gains toward 6.6640 against the US dollar. Currency pairs reflect the relative valuation of domestic monetary units against foreign reserves.
stories.a: China's bank wealth management assets scaled 35.4 trillion yuan. Concurrently, UOB strategists mapped a trajectory for the Chinese yuan toward 6.6640 against the US dollar. Cross-border capital flows continue to reprice as onshore institutional asset pools adjust to the prevailing carry differentials.

stories.t: National AI Fund Deployments and IPOs
stories.b: China's national AI fund deployed a massive 600 billion yuan pool into various technology ventures. A fund is a large pool of money collected from different investors to buy assets. At the same time, DeepSeek moved closer to executing what would be China's largest initial public offering financing in history. An initial public offering happens when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time.
stories.i: China's national AI fund deployed a 600 billion yuan allocation across target enterprises. Concurrently, DeepSeek advanced toward what stands as China's largest initial public offering financing in history. Primary market liquidity channels remain heavily concentrated in domestic tech heavyweights.
stories.a: China's national AI fund disbursed capital from its 600 billion yuan vehicle into targeted tech enterprises. Simultaneously, DeepSeek approached completion on what marks China's largest initial public offering financing to date. Underwriter syndicates are pricing the equity blocks against heightened scrutiny in global risk assets.

politics.b: China's bank wealth management market reached 35.4 trillion yuan. The national AI fund deployed 600 billion yuan. DeepSeek neared a record initial public offering.
politics.i: China's bank wealth management market scaled 35.4 trillion yuan. The national AI fund deployed 600 billion yuan across sector targets. DeepSeek approached a record initial public offering.
politics.a: China's bank wealth management sector reached 35.4 trillion yuan. The national AI fund deployed 600 billion yuan into target assets. DeepSeek neared the largest initial public offering financing in Chinese corporate history.

timeline: China's bank wealth management market reached 35.4 trillion yuan.
UOB outlined a yuan trajectory toward 6.6640 against the US dollar.
Details emerged regarding investments made by the 600-billion-yuan national AI fund.

India.label: India
India.sub: Sensex slides as oil prices surge and inflation jumps

stories.t: Sensex Extends Losing Streak as Oil Prices and Inflation Surge
stories.src: The Indian Awaaz · Business Today · BBN Times
stories.b: The BSE SENSEX dropped 460 points to 73,249.39 for a third consecutive decline. Brent crude oil surpassed $111 per barrel, reaching a five-month high. Wholesale price inflation surged to 11.39%. This means the rate at which wholesale prices go up across the economy increased sharply.
stories.i: The BSE SENSEX dropped 460 points to 73,249.39, marking its third consecutive session of losses while the Nifty slipped below 22,700. Brent crude surpassed $111 per barrel to touch a five-month high, driving wholesale price inflation to 11.39%. These surging commodity costs compounded broader pressures on domestic equities.
stories.a: The BSE SENSEX fell 460 points to 73,249.39 as the Nifty breached support at 22,700, extending the losing streak to a third day. Brent crude breached $111 per barrel to hit a five-month high, directly accelerating wholesale price inflation to 11.39%. This energy shock complicates macroeconomic stability as transmission channels price higher imported fuel costs directly into domestic industrial inputs.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Announces 3-Day Variable Rate Repo Auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India announced a Variable Rate Repo auction for October 23, 2026. A repo auction is when the central bank lends money to commercial banks. The central bank will provide 50,000 crore rupees through a three-day window. This action manages short-term liquidity conditions in the financial system.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a three-day Variable Rate Repo auction for October 23, 2026, to manage near-term liquidity conditions. The central bank will allot 50,000 crore rupees through the liquidity adjustment facility window. This operation allows financial institutions to borrow short-term funds until the reversal date on October 26, 2026.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India deployed a 50,000 crore rupee three-day Variable Rate Repo auction under the liquidity adjustment facility for October 23, 2026, responding to evolving near-term cash conditions. Counterparties will access funds through the morning window with a reversal date set for October 26, 2026. This fine-tuning operation manages interbank rate pressures as short-term liquidity fluctuates.

stories.t: RBI Sets Final Redemption Price for Sovereign Gold Bonds
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India set the final redemption price for the Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-II. These bonds reach the end of their eight-year term on October 23, 2026. Investors receive payouts based on the official scheme terms established by the government.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India established the final redemption price for the Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-II. The tranche reaches maturity on October 23, 2026, exactly eight years after its original issue date. Payouts follow the calculation methodology outlined in the original government notification from October 2018.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India finalized the redemption price for the Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-II ahead of the eight-year maturity date on October 23, 2026. The cash-settled repayment liquidates the specific tranche issued under the government framework dated October 8, 2018. This concludes the lifecycle for holders of this particular sovereign debt series.

politics.b: Political leaders face economic pressure as oil import costs climb. Higher fuel prices affect everyday consumer goods across the country. Government officials monitor financial market volatility closely.
politics.i: Rising oil prices increase import bills and complicate fiscal management for policymakers. Escalating commodity costs feed directly into wholesale inflation figures. Authorities face simultaneous pressures from currency depreciation and equity market declines.
politics.a: Surging international crude benchmarks amplify external sector vulnerabilities and strain the fiscal deficit through higher subsidy burdens. Policymakers confront compounding macroeconomic headwinds from accelerated wholesale price inflation and capital outflows. Exchange rate depreciation against the US dollar adds further strain to domestic monetary management.

timeline: Sovereign Gold Bond 2018-19 Series-II was issued
Sensex fell 460 points and WPI inflation surged to 11.39%

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras and elections drive Brazilian markets

stories.t: Ibovespa declines amid presidential runoff
stories.b: The main stock market index in Brazil, called the Ibovespa, dropped by 1.5%. A stock market index tracks the value of a group of important companies. Investors are people who put money into companies to make a profit. They are feeling nervous because of the upcoming presidential runoff vote.
stories.i: The Ibovespa index fell by 1.5% as political risk weighed on sentiment. Investors reduced their exposure ahead of the presidential runoff. Market participants monitored whether the index would hold above the 202,259 support level.
stories.a: The Ibovespa shed 1.5% as election uncertainty compounded domestic risk premiums. Price action tested the 202,259 technical support floor. Market participants priced in heightened volatility ahead of the presidential runoff.

stories.t: Petrobras targeted by pension talks and new oil find
stories.src: The Star · Valor International · AD HOC NEWS
stories.b: Petrobras is a big oil company in Brazil. An adviser said the company will not be privatized, which means it will stay owned partly by the government. The company is trying to fix a huge pension deficit of 42bn Brazilian reals. A pension is money paid to workers when they retire. Bank of America raised its price target for Petrobras shares to $28.00.
stories.i: Petrobras sought a deal to address its R$42bn Petros pension deficit. An adviser confirmed that Bolsonaro plans to unleash Petrobras without pursuing privatisation. Bank of America raised its target for Petrobras stock to USD 28.00 after the company made a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa.
stories.a: Petrobras engaged in negotiations regarding its R$42bn Petros pension shortfall. An adviser ruled out outright privatisation under a potential Bolsonaro administration, focusing instead on operational expansion. Bank of America lifted its equity price target to USD 28.00 following a fresh hydrocarbon discovery off the coast of Amapa.

politics.b: Investors are watching the upcoming presidential runoff election very closely. Political uncertainty is causing the stock market to drop. Advisers are discussing how candidates will handle state-run companies like Petrobras.
politics.i: The presidential runoff introduces high political risk into domestic asset valuations. Market sentiment remains fragile as investors evaluate future governance for state-controlled entities. Political campaigns continue to shape sector-specific stock movements.
politics.a: Electoral dynamics in the presidential runoff dictate current risk appetite across Brazilian equities. Political friction amplifies cash-flow uncertainty for state-backed enterprises. Market participants price policy continuity risks directly into local indices.

timeline: 22 Oct
Petrobras makes a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco headquarters evacuated after regional escalations

stories.t: Aramco Evacuates Headquarters Following Regional Attacks
stories.src: Reuters via يمن مونيتور · Modern Ghana · The Economic Times
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is the state-owned oil company of Saudi Arabia. It is one of the biggest businesses in the world. Saudi Aramco told its employees to leave its headquarters in Dhahran and work from home. This happened after fighting escalated in Yemen and attacks targeted Saudi locations. Two people died in an attack at a Saudi airport.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco ordered staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and transition to remote work. The decision followed escalating fighting involving Yemen and strikes targeting domestic infrastructure, including airports. Two individuals died during the attack at a Saudi airport.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco initiated a full evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters, directing personnel to remote operations amid mounting security risks. Operational continuity faced immediate disruption as strikes targeted Riyadh, domestic airports, and the Shaybah oilfield. The physical security breaches compound operational challenges for the state-backed oil producer.

stories.t: Oil Producer Seeks Stockpile Expansion and Shaybah Field Targeted
stories.src: Iran International · BBN Times · Energy Intelligence
stories.b: Saudi Aramco wants to buy more oil storage space overseas. This plan follows a recent war involving Iran. Separately, Houthi forces targeted the massive Shaybah oil field. These events added pressure to global oil markets.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco sought to expand its overseas oil stockpiles following the Iran war. Houthi forces launched a targeted strike on the giant Shaybah oil field. The attacks contributed to broader equity market declines, including a drop in Germany's DAX 40 index.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco pursued international oil storage expansion strategies in the wake of the Iran conflict. Houthi operational targeting extended to the prolific Shaybah field, amplifying supply security premiums. These geopolitical shocks transmitted directly into European equities, driving the DAX 40 down by 1.07% to 25,371.75.

politics.b: The International Monetary Fund stated that recent attacks by Houthi forces had a limited impact on the overall economy of Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile, the European Parliament urged officials to list the Houthis as a terrorist organization. The United States also decided to pull some of its diplomats out of Saudi Arabia.
politics.i: The International Monetary Fund assessed that Houthi attacks generated a limited impact on the Saudi economy. The European Parliament urged a terrorist designation for the Houthis. Concurrently, the United States withdrew select diplomatic personnel from the country.
politics.a: The International Monetary Fund evaluated the macroeconomic toll of Houthi strikes as restricted in magnitude for the Saudi economy. Diplomatic pressure mounted as the European Parliament pressed for a terrorist classification of the Houthi movement. The United States enacted a partial withdrawal of its diplomatic staff from the kingdom.

timeline: Aramco asked employees to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira exchange rates, stock losses and monetary policy

stories.t: Naira Slumps as Dollar Demand Grows
stories.b: The Nigerian currency, called the naira, hit N1,369 for a US dollar. People wanted more US dollars to make payments. The currency hit N1,370 at the bureau de change window.
stories.i: The naira touched N1,369 per US dollar as demand for dollar payments surged. The currency subsequently weakened to N1,370 per US dollar at the bureau de change window.
stories.a: The naira depreciated to N1,369 against the US dollar amid rising demand for foreign exchange settlement. Spot transactions at the bureau de change window later printed at N1,370 per US dollar.

stories.t: Stock Exchange Extends Losses
stories.b: The main stock market index fell by 0.07%. Investors lost N104bn in value. Share prices dropped across the board.
stories.i: The NGXASI extended its losses by dropping 0.07%. Equity investors lost a total of N104bn during the session.
stories.a: The NGXASI index declined by 0.07%, extending the broader market correction. Aggregate investor wealth contracted by N104bn.

stories.t: Currency Outside Banks Reaches N4.92trn
stories.b: Central bank data showed that physical cash held outside the banking system reached N4.92trn in September. This counts all the money people keep out of bank accounts.
stories.i: Data from the central bank showed that currency outside banks climbed to N4.92trn in September. This metric tracks physical money circulating outside the formal banking system.
stories.a: Central bank figures indicated that currency outside banks reached N4.92trn in September. The monetary aggregate reflects cash retained outside institutional vaults.

politics.b: Former leaders and company chiefs debated the economic policies of President Tinubu. Obasanjo stated that the currency devaluation made citizens poorer and created high poverty. Meanwhile, the chairman of Airtel praised the foreign exchange reforms for building investor confidence.
politics.i: Former President Obasanjo criticized President Tinubu's foreign exchange reforms, arguing that the overnight devaluation of the naira increased poverty levels. Conversely, the chairman of Airtel praised the administration's currency reforms for bolstering investor confidence.
politics.a: Former President Obasanjo asserted that the sudden devaluation of the naira under President Tinubu exacerbated national poverty metrics. In contrast, Airtel's chairman lauded the foreign exchange reforms for attracting positive investor sentiment.

timeline: The naira traded at N1,369 per US dollar before weakening to N1,370 at bureau de change outlets.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian shares face losses as oil jumps and Wall Street drops

stories.t: Australian Shares Decline Following Wall Street Tech Drops and Oil Surges
stories.b: The Australian stock market is expected to open lower today. This drop follows heavy losses for technology companies on the American stock market known as the Nasdaq. At the same time, the price of crude oil climbed past $112 per barrel to reach its highest level since May.
stories.i: Local equities face downward pressure as the ASX 200 tracks a sharp sell-off in American technology shares on the Nasdaq. Meanwhile, Brent crude pushed past $112 a barrel to touch its highest valuation since May.
stories.a: Australian index futures point to a soft open following an aggressive tech-led liquidation on the Nasdaq that marked its worst single-session decline since June. Concurrently, Brent crude breached $112 per barrel to print its highest price point since May, compounding macro headwinds for risk assets.

stories.t: Newmont Reports Q3 Financial Growth Amid Sector Updates
stories.b: Mining company Newmont announced higher adjusted net income and sales for the third quarter. Other small-cap companies also released updates, including Solis Minerals preparing for drilling at Cucho. Alkane delivered a solid quarter while XSO slipped.
stories.i: Newmont posted positive third-quarter adjusted net income and sales figures. Across the small-cap sector, Solis Minerals advanced preparations for Cucho drilling activities, and Alkane reported a solid operational quarter.
stories.a: Newmont delivered an expansion in third-quarter adjusted net income and top-line sales. In the junior resources space, Solis Minerals laid groundwork for Cucho drilling operations, while Alkane printed a robust quarterly report and XSO edged lower.

politics.b: There is no major political news reported in the market updates for Australia today.
politics.i: No significant political developments were registered across Australian market feeds for the session.
politics.a: Domestic policy and governmental actions remained absent from the operational news flow affecting Australian equities.

Brent crude climbed past $112 per barrel to hit its highest price since May.
